tool.name: Clank – AI Studio
tool.description: AI studio: chats with projects and templates, folders and repositories, images, music, video, group chat, documents, schedules, MCP, transcripts and voice assistant.
tool.long_description: Works with the assistants connected in OmniWrench (Settings > AI assistants) and shares chats and projects with the chat panel. Every project gets its own workspace: local folders, Git repositories and online repositories (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps – read online or cloned locally). Assistants can list, search and read the workspace, see Git status, log and diffs, propose file changes (shown as a diff) and run commands (shown with an explanation) – both only after confirmation, with an option to remember the answer for the session. What assistants may see is set on the page 'AI access' like for every tool; pseudonymization replaces addresses and names before sending. Files open in a viewer with highlighting and can be attached to the chat. The "Images" tab creates images with the connected image providers (OpenAI, Gemini, xAI, Black Forest Labs, fal.ai, Replicate, Stability AI, Ideogram, Recraft, MiniMax), optionally with reference images; the gallery shows the images of the AI data storage. In the "Group chat" several assistants discuss a topic in turn – with brakes for rounds, contributions, length, time and tokens, pause per round, stop on agreement or repetition, interjections and a summary. The "Music" and "Video" tabs create tracks and clips (Gemini Lyria/Omni Flash, ElevenLabs, MiniMax, Stability, Mureka, xAI, Runway, Luma, Seedance, fal.ai, Replicate and more), play them and edit them with ffmpeg: trim, convert to MP3 or GIF, add music to a video, remove sound, save a still. On Windows Clank downloads ffmpeg on request. Plus: templates for recurring questions (with placeholders), screenshots straight into the chat, documents written with the assistant and exported as HTML, PDF or ODT, and schedules that ask the assistant questions at fixed times. The "MCP" tab connects external MCP servers, and OmniWrench offers its own functions to other AI programs as a local MCP server (token, changes confirmed here in the program). "Transcript" transcribes meetings from microphone and system sound live – only with the consent of all participants, with speaker recognition, optional speaker profiles and a summary; the text is stored, never the recording. The "Voice assistant" listens offline for a wake word ("Hey Clank"), records the question and reads the answer aloud.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.intro: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI programs with tools. At the top, external MCP servers can be connected so that the assistants can use their tools. At the bottom, OmniWrench itself can be switched on as an MCP server for other AI programs (e.g. Claude Desktop, VS Code).
mcp.col.name: Name
mcp.client_hint: The tools are available to the assistants in AI Studio and in the chat panel while AI Studio is open. The AI access level of AI Studio applies: read-only tools from level 3 (read), all others from level 4 and only after confirmation.
mcp.server_hint: The server is only reachable on this computer (127.0.0.1) and requires the token. It runs while AI Studio is open. It offers the functions the built-in assistants have, with the same access levels and the same pseudonymization. A separate level for external programs can be set under "AI access" → exceptions → "MCP server". Changes are always confirmed here in the program.

ts.consent.title: Consent before recording
ts.consent.head: Conversations may only be recorded with the consent of everyone involved.
ts.consent.body:
Secretly recording non-public speech is a criminal offence in Germany (§ 201 StGB) and prohibited in many other countries. Under the GDPR, processing needs a legal basis, usually the consent of all participants.

During recording, the microphone and/or system audio are sent in parts to "{provider}" and converted to text there. To tell speakers apart, voice features are computed on this computer (in memory only). The text is saved, not the recording.

Speaker profiles (permanently stored voice features with names) are biometric data. They are only created if allowed below and the person concerned has explicitly agreed; they are always stored encrypted.
ts.consent.agree: All participants have been informed and agree to recording and transcription.
ts.consent.profiles: Use and create speaker profiles (only with the explicit consent of those concerned)
ts.consent.profiles_always: Always use and create speaker profiles, without the separate notice
ts.pnotice.title: Store speaker profiles permanently
ts.pnotice.head: Voice profiles are biometric data (Art. 9 GDPR).
ts.pnotice.body:
A speaker profile permanently stores voice characteristics of a person together with their name, so the person can be recognised in later recordings. Under Art. 9 GDPR such data belongs to the special categories of personal data and may generally only be processed with the explicit consent of the person concerned.

You alone as the user are responsible for the lawfulness. OmniWrench stores the profiles encrypted and only on this computer; they can be deleted at any time under “Speaker profiles”. Data subjects have the right of access and erasure.
ts.pnotice.accept: I have read this notice, will obtain the required consents and take responsibility.
ts.consent.notice: Notice: this conversation is being recorded to create a transcript and converted to text with an AI service. Please object briefly if you do not agree.

ts.profiles.hint: Saved voices with names. Known voices are named automatically in new transcripts. Profiles are stored encrypted and can be deleted here at any time.
